You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC

1. Treat each instance independently. Read its test grid, task id, action choices, and remaining demo/attempt caps. On every turn, choose exactly one puzzle action and make that action JSON object the final line; avoid narration and unrelated tool calls because neither advances the puzzle nor supplies evidence. Reassess after each demo or submission feedback.
2. Infer the transformation from demonstrations and the test grid. Separate observed facts from hypotheses, and check that the examples actually cover the test's structure. When they do not, do not turn a plausible pattern into a confident rule.
3. Request one more demo when its likely information can distinguish live hypotheses and is worth its one-point cost. Incorporate that pair before deciding again; don't request repeatedly without reassessing whether another example can change the answer. Compare this cost with the one-point cost of a wrong submission and the remaining caps.
4. Submit a complete grid when the rule is sufficiently supported; verify dimensions (1–30) and cell values (0–9). Use `finish` only after the instance is over, and stop when the instance has ended.

# Continual-ARC learned patterns

## Patterned recoloring / shape search
- In one ARC instance, the input used background color 9, candidate cells color 0, and a 3-cell marker color 7.
- The 7 marker was an L-shaped triomino in a 2x2 box: top-right plus both bottom cells (`.X / XX`).
- Rule inferred and validated: find every exact placement of this triomino among zeros (apparently using the marker's orientation), recolor the three matching zero cells to 7, and leave unmatched zeros and all other cells unchanged. Existing marker stays as-is.
- Important: placements can overlap larger connected zero regions; match the precise three-cell shape rather than recoloring an entire connected component. Example: the upper-left zero component had an extra cell, but only its matching three-cell subset became 7.
- The test submission following this rule was marked CORRECT.

## Binary mask panel removes cells while recoloring (validated 2026-09-29; task-f34bd08d)
A vertical separator divides a left source panel from a same-sized right mask panel. In the demo, the left panel was 6x12 with foreground 6/background 0; separator color 7; right panel background 3 with holes (0). In the test, panels were 16x13; left foreground 3/background 0; separator 4; right background 9 with holes 0. Output is just the left panel: change every source foreground cell to color 2, except erase (leave 0) any position where the right panel has a hole 0. Preserve source-background zeros. The mask overlays position-for-position (same row and local column), not reflected or shifted. The inferred rule was validated by a correct submission. Procedure: locate the full-height separator, split into equal-width panels; for each left cell, output 2 iff the left cell is the foreground color and the corresponding right-panel cell is not 0; otherwise output 0. Return only the transformed left panel (omit separator and mask).

## Fill between consecutive marker pairs along rows and columns (validated 2026-09-29; task-9aa51737)
Three demos and the test establish this rule: identify the marker color (e.g. color 2 in demos 1 and 3, color 7 in demo 2 and the test). In every row and every column, consider marker occurrences in order. For each two consecutive markers on that line, recolor every cell strictly between them to color 3. Preserve the markers, and leave background cells outside such bounded intervals unchanged. Apply both horizontal and vertical fills; where the intervals intersect, the result is still 3. The test used a 23x27 field of 6 with sparse 7 markers; fill 6s between consecutive 7s in any row or column with 3. A submission generated by this rule was confirmed CORRECT.

Efficient check for a background cell: recolor it if there are marker cells on both sides in its row with no intervening marker between the nearest bracketing pair, or similarly above and below in its column. Do not fill before the first marker or after the last marker, and do not change marker cells.

# Continual-ARC observations

## Extend aligned same-color rays, paying attention to blocked directions

Observed in task `task-2a0c99b3`: input had background 6, three 3s at (1-based) r4c9, r5c10, r6c10, and two 7s at r6c11, r7c12, plus a 4 at r5c11. Correct output added 3s at r1c6, r2c7, r3c8 (continuing the collinear r4c9-r5c10 line backward/up-left) and 7s at r8c13, r9c14 (continuing the 7 pair down-right). Other cells stayed unchanged. The added line extensions terminate at the grid edge. The 3 line's forward down-right continuation is blocked by the 7 at r6c11, so examine both endpoints/directions and blockers rather than extending only one direction or assuming every apparent same-color sequence is vertical. Verify full grid dimensions carefully before submission.

General lesson from demonstrations: these tasks often extend a same-color straight/diagonal line from its existing marked segment to a boundary; the segment orientation and unobstructed direction matter. A demonstrated line may be extended only on the open side, so preserve the seed cells and check whether another color blocks continuation.

## 3x3 symbol-tile reduction

Observed in task-da40e4c0 (two demos and a correct test): input grid dimensions were 3× the output dimensions. Split the input into aligned, non-overlapping 3×3 tiles. Each tile uses 5 as its background and may contain 0 noise/empty cells plus a symbol color (e.g. 1, 3, 8, 9). Output one cell per tile: the symbol color present in that tile; if there is no symbol color, output 0. Preserve tile order and make the output dimensions input-height/3 × input-width/3.

Evidence: demo 1 reduced 9×9 to 3×3 with an 8-symbol tile becoming 8 and other tiles 0; demo 2 reduced 24×24 to 8×8; the 12×12 test reduced to [[0,0,0,0],[3,9,0,1],[9,8,1,3],[0,9,9,0]], which was accepted. This was one task, so verify the background/symbol convention against future examples before assuming every 3×3 reduction follows it.
